flood.en: Move stock & records higher, protect documents, back up data.
flood.hi: सामान व कागज़ात ऊँचाई पर रखें।

heat.en: Shift heavy work to cooler hours, keep drinking water ready, check power backup.
heat.hi: दोपहर में काम कम करें, पानी रखें।
heat.mr: दुपारी काम कमी करा, पाणी ठेवा.

drought.en: Store water, check stock of water-dependent supplies, plan for shortages.

storm.en: Tie down loose items, close shutters, charge phones, back up data.
storm.hi: खुला सामान बाँधें, शटर बंद रखें।
storm.mr: सैल वस्तू बांधा, शटर बंद ठेवा.

cold_wave.en: Protect staff and cold-sensitive stock, check heating and pipes.
cold_wave.hi: कर्मचारी व माल ठंड से बचाएँ।

owner: Check that drains and gutters around the premises are clear
Note which stock, machines and records sit at floor level
Keep important documents together in a waterproof bag
bank: Note the borrower for follow-up if the forecast worsens
Check that insurance details for stock and collateral are on file
No action on the account is needed at this stage

owner: Move stock, machines and records to a higher shelf or floor
Keep important documents in a waterproof bag
Plan to switch off main power if water enters
Back up billing and stock data to your phone or cloud
bank: Call the borrower to confirm they received the warning
Check insurance cover on stock and collateral
Pre-approve eligible relief (bridge loan / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Mark account for follow-up after the event

owner: Move stock, machines and records to the highest safe place now
Switch off main power before water enters, and do not touch wet equipment
Take documents, cash and phones with you if you are told to leave
Do not stay to protect goods: people come first
bank: Call the borrower today to confirm they are safe and received the warning
Review eligibility for relief (bridge loan / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Prepare the insurance claim checklist for the borrower
Schedule a follow-up visit after the event

owner: Check that fans, coolers and drinking water are available for staff
Note which stock is sensitive to heat
Check that power backup is working
bank: Note the borrower for follow-up if the forecast worsens
Check whether the business depends on refrigeration or outdoor work
No action on the account is needed at this stage

owner: Shift heavy and outdoor work to early morning or evening
Keep drinking water and shade available for staff
Move heat-sensitive stock to the coolest place you have
Test power backup, as outages are more likely
bank: Call the borrower to confirm they received the warning
Ask about spoilage or lost working hours that could affect cash flow
Review eligibility for short-term working-capital support per bank policy
Mark account for follow-up after the event

owner: Stop outdoor and heavy work during the hottest hours (12 to 4 pm)
Make sure every worker has water, shade and rest breaks
Move or sell heat-sensitive stock before it spoils
Know the signs of heatstroke and the nearest health centre
bank: Call the borrower today to confirm they received the warning
Review eligibility for relief (working-capital support / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Check insurance cover on perishable stock
Schedule a follow-up after the event

owner: Check how many days of water your business has stored
Fix leaking taps, tanks and pipes
List supplies whose price or availability depends on rain
bank: Note the borrower for follow-up if conditions worsen
Check how much the business depends on water or farm inputs
No action on the account is needed at this stage

owner: Store extra water and reduce non-essential use
Stock up on key supplies before prices rise
Talk to suppliers about delivery during shortages
Plan for lower sales if your customers depend on farming
bank: Call the borrower to confirm they received the warning
Ask about input costs and expected sales over the next season
Review eligibility for restructuring or working-capital support per bank policy
Mark account for follow-up next month

owner: Arrange an alternative water source such as a tanker or shared storage
Cut water-heavy work to the minimum your business needs
Agree payment and delivery terms with suppliers early
Ask your bank about support before cash runs short
bank: Call the borrower today to discuss cash flow for the season
Review eligibility for relief (restructuring / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Check for government drought-relief schemes the borrower can use
Schedule a monthly follow-up until conditions ease

owner: Check the roof, signboards and shutters for loose parts
Note what is kept outdoors and could be blown away
Keep a torch and charged power bank ready
bank: Note the borrower for follow-up if the forecast worsens
Check that insurance details for the premises are on file
No action on the account is needed at this stage

owner: Tie down or bring inside anything kept outdoors
Close and secure shutters, windows and roof sheets
Charge phones and back up billing and stock data
Keep important documents in a waterproof bag
bank: Call the borrower to confirm they received the warning
Check insurance cover on premises, stock and collateral
Pre-approve eligible relief (bridge loan / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Mark account for follow-up after the event

owner: Close the business early and send staff home before the storm arrives
Secure shutters and switch off main power
Take documents, cash and phones with you
Stay indoors, away from windows, trees and power lines
bank: Call the borrower today to confirm they are safe and received the warning
Review eligibility for relief (bridge loan / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Prepare the insurance claim checklist for the borrower
Schedule a follow-up visit after the event

owner: Check that staff have warm clothing and a heated or sheltered place
Note which stock or machines are sensitive to cold
Check heaters and wiring for safety
bank: Note the borrower for follow-up if the forecast worsens
Check whether the business depends on outdoor work or cold-sensitive stock
No action on the account is needed at this stage

owner: Shift outdoor work to the warmer hours of the day
Protect cold-sensitive stock, plants or animals with covers
Insulate exposed water pipes and tanks
Never use coal or charcoal heaters in a closed room
bank: Call the borrower to confirm they received the warning
Ask about lost working days or damaged stock
Review eligibility for short-term support per bank policy
Mark account for follow-up after the event

owner: Stop outdoor work in the early morning and at night
Make sure every worker has warm clothing and hot drinks
Move cold-sensitive stock indoors or cover it
Never use coal or charcoal heaters in a closed room
bank: Call the borrower today to confirm they received the warning
Review eligibility for relief (short-term support / EMI deferment) per bank policy
Check insurance cover on stock or livestock
Schedule a follow-up after the event

flood: Move food stock and packaging off the floor and discard anything flood water touches
Wrap fabric and finished goods in plastic and store them off the floor

drought: Prioritise water for the most valuable crop or stock
cold_wave: Cover seedlings and young plants overnight
